Summary: The paper benchmarks strategies for writing OMIM-style phenotype entries from exactly the papers the curators cited (100 entries with 2–12 references; 515 papers, 19% readable in full by open access), with one model (Claude Opus 5.5) fixed as writer, extractor, auditor and judge. The strategies span read and write (direct reading, an agentic curator), extract then write (an evidence graph, a case table) and memory first (recall, then verify), plus a memory-only control, three add-ons and four reading-better variants of direct reading. The primary endpoint is model-judged recall of 6,652 atomic facts split once, without sight of any draft, from OMIM's variant-centred allelic-variant text as deposited in ClinVar. Findings: (i) hiding the full text of the same papers lowers coverage from 79.8% to 36.1% (+43.7 points, 95% CI 38.3–49.1, 46 entries; Sec. 4.1, Fig. 2a, Table 24); (ii) at the main settings, on the 93 entries every strategy completed, no design conveyed more than direct reading (agent −0.6, evidence graph −0.5, case table −1.9; Table 1), and the order shifts with the entries averaged and the extraction settings (App. F, Table 21); (iii) on 38 held-out entries a completeness pass adds 2.6 points (1.7–3.6) while lengthening drafts from 10,802 to 14,412 characters, and on all 41 the gain holds only if the unrevised draft is kept where the safety filter stopped the revision (Sec. 4.3, Tables 30, 32, 34); (iv) the claim-level audit catches citation swaps and blunt single-value substitutions but, under its best-verdict rule, no added citation (0/30) and, by construction, no omission (Sec. 4.5, Fig. 4, Tables 50–53). All three reviewers score the paper 5 and recommend rejection with confidence 4. They agree that the experimental control, the within-paper access manipulation, the handling of safety-filter stops and the disclosure of post hoc choices are well above the norm for LLM-pipeline comparisons. They also agree that the comparative claims rest on a judge from the writer's own model family that no person validated, that the strategy comparison runs in a regime (small inputs, mostly abstracts, one long-context model, unmatched extraction settings) where parity is close to expected, that the reading-better gains are confounded with draft length, and that the benchmark cannot be reused with comparable numbers because the fact lists are not released and fresh-split stability is unmeasured.
Strengths: Clean single-variable design. Model, supplied papers, guards, audit, scoring and the fact lists are held fixed and only the strategy varies (Fig. 1; Secs. 3.2–3.3). Fact lists are fixed once without sight of any draft, which avoids the per-draft re-splitting artefact that runs 2–5 points higher (Table 6; App. M.4). Comparisons are paired over entries with percentile bootstrap intervals, better/worse/tied counts and exact sign tests, with Holm adjustment for secondary measures (Tables 7–8).

The access effect comes from a within-paper manipulation, not an observational contrast. The same 91 full-text papers are hidden, the same 2,120 facts are scored, every arm is unrepaired, and full text is better on 45 of 46 entries and tied on 1 (Sec. 4.1; Table 24). The cross-paper by-access table is correctly treated as confounded with era and journal (Table 13). Second-hand passages are measured as a partial substitute (+4.9 points), and passage-based claims are checked against the full text (App. G).

Safety-filter stops are treated as an outcome rather than silently dropped. The symmetric completion rule, completion tables (Tables 5, 29, 45, 55) and intention-to-treat sensitivity analyses (Tables 11, 32) show that a stopped reply costs a one-call strategy the whole entry but a per-paper strategy one paper. The earlier 2.1-point evidence-graph deficit that this rule corrected is documented (App. M.4). This is a transferable measurement lesson that LLM-pipeline comparisons rarely report.

Unusually transparent reporting of analysis status. Section 3.3 lists every choice made after results were seen, items (a)–(i), and App. Tables 2–3 give each experiment's entry set, status and dropouts. Deviations from design are documented (Apps. J, K, L), and the wording is careful: no equivalence claim without a margin (Sec. 4.2), the case-table deficit called 'suggestive', and runs on 10 or fewer entries labelled exploratory (Sec. 4.4).

Measurement uncertainty is reported beside effects. Judge variation and run-to-run replicates on 30 entries (App. E, Table 20) give a 95% half-width of 1.0 point over 93 entries and are used as a yardstick, not a test. They also show that the evidence graph's sign flips between the 30 replicate entries and the 93 main entries because of entry selection, not replicate noise.

Sensible contamination controls. The memory-only control is reported by creation era, and entries created in 2026 were held out from all development: on the 20 compared, memory conveys 7.0% of facts against 52.2% for direct reading (App. M.2). Header-only causal-gene F1 falls from 88.9–100% in the four older bands to 41.2% from 620000 on and 30.0% on the 2026 entries (Table 16; App. M.2). The paper explicitly does not claim that reading is free of memorisation.

The audit blind-spot analysis is concrete and actionable. Under the best-verdict-over-cited-papers rule, none of 30 added irrelevant citations was flagged although the added paper's own verdict was 'unsupported' on all 176 claims attributed to it (Sec. 4.5; Table 50). Deleted zygosity and 'one family' qualifiers pass (Table 51), and real multi-citation paragraphs contain 4–7% non-supporting (claim, cited paper) pairs (Table 53).

Completion, model calls, tokens and list-price cost are reported per strategy and experiment (Tables 5, 12, 34, 42, 48, 49), draft length is reported beside coverage gains (Sec. 4.3), and every deviation of the released pipelines from their defaults is documented (App. J, Tables 37–39).
Weaknesses: No human validation of any measurement, and every judgement comes from the writer's own model family (all three reviewers). Fact splitting, the conveyed/partly/absent verdicts, the 'stated in the supplied text' label, the audit, the completeness check and the re-examination of draft–reference disagreements are all made by Claude Opus 5.5 (Sec. 3.2; Limitation (i)). The only reliability evidence is self-consistency (95.7% agreement between two judgings; App. E). The comparative effects are 0.5–1.9 points in the main comparison (Table 1) and 1.6–3.3 points for reading better (Table 30), the size most exposed to systematic judge leniency or self-preference (Panickssery et al., cited in Sec. 2). A stratified expert-labelled sample with chance-corrected agreement, and a judge from another family, are needed for the claims to rest on more than one model's judgement.

The tested regime largely predetermines the null result between strategies, and the regime where designs should separate was not compared (all three reviewers). Entries have 2–12 references, 81% of papers are abstract or title only, and 2,669 of 6,239 compared facts are not stated in any supplied text (Table 19; Sec. 5). The padding entries' unpadded inputs have a median of 39,450 characters (Table 44, 6 entries; no input-size distribution is reported for the 100 main entries). Padding used unrelated papers that no draft cited and left 2 entries under the primary rule (Sec. 4.4; App. K.1), every large entry lost at least one strategy to stopped replies (App. K.2), and the 30–75-reference tier gives no findings (App. M.1). With one long-context writer and no smaller-context condition (Limitation (ii)), 'no design beat direct reading' mostly confirms long-context results already in the literature, and the title, abstract and conclusion do not foreground this regime dependence.

The main comparison is not matched on settings, and each paradigm has one implementation (all three reviewers). Writers run at high effort, but per-paper extraction in the evidence graph and case table runs at medium effort with synopsis terms (and the table's inheritance) assigned by rule (Sec. 3.2). The matched ablation is post hoc, uses 38 entries chosen with more full text and changes two factors at once (App. F, Table 21); under it the case table moves from −2.3 to −0.2 points and the matched evidence graph is +1.8 (+0.4 to +3.3) above direct reading. The agentic curator's paper opening is self-reported and its tool calls are not logged (App. B). The case table's 'suggestive deficit' therefore describes this implementation at these settings, not the paradigm.

The primary endpoint is recall-only, so the reading-better gains cannot be separated from writing more (all three reviewers). The completeness pass adds 2.6 points while drafts grow from 10,802 to 14,412 characters and checkable claims from 129 to 164 per audited entry (Sec. 4.3, Table 34). The three-draft merge gains +3.1 partly on facts the text does not state while adding unsupported and contradicted claims and lowering variant precision from 87.1% to 83.4% (Sec. 4.3, Table 33). Extract-then-write drafts also say more (113.5 and 117.9 audited claims against 101.0; Table 1). The only precision-side check is the same model's audit on 20 entries with no interval (Table 33), and no length-matched baseline is run (Limitation (iv)).

Construct validity of the endpoint is narrow, and the access effect is partly a property of the reference (all three reviewers). Strategies write whole phenotype entries, but the reference is variant-centred allelic-variant text from OMIM gene entries (Sec. 3.1); only 327 of 515 papers have an in-scope paragraph, and about 24% of a direct-reading draft's statements have a counterpart in the reference (App. H; Limitation (v)). Variant notation, zygosity and counts usually sit in full text: the supplied text states 76% of full-text-paper facts but 26% of abstract-only facts (1,246/1,639 and 1,099/4,221; Fig. 2b, Table 19). The paper itself calls the effect expected (Sec. 1), and without a breakdown by fact type the +43.7 points mainly shows that abstracts lack variant details, which adds little qualitatively to prior full-text versus abstract text-mining results (Westergaard et al., 2018, cited).

Missingness from safety-filter stops is outcome-dependent and its relation to entry difficulty is untested (all three reviewers). Seven of 100 main entries drop out unevenly by strategy (Table 5), 10 of 30 entries created in 2026 (Table 55), every large entry (App. K.2) and all of STORM (App. J). Intention to treat moves the agent from −0.6 to +0.4 and widens the case table's interval to include zero (Table 11); the completeness arms fall to −3.5 and −4.8 when lost entries count as zero (Table 32). The three entries the completeness pass lost are exactly the three on which the evidence graph lost a paper (App. I; Table 5), which points to content-specific triggers. No analysis tests whether completion correlates with era, number of papers, full-text share, disease area or direct reading's coverage on the same entries.

Two analysis choices that apply to every result were made after results were seen, the main strategies were developed on their evaluation entries, and much of the narrative rests on post hoc or very small analyses (all three reviewers). Fixed fact lists and the symmetric rule were adopted after a first analysis had put the evidence graph 2.1 points below direct reading (Sec. 3.3 items (a)–(b); App. M.4), and held-out evidence is limited to 20 compared 2026 entries and the 41-entry reading-better split (Limitation (ix)). The stated/not-stated restrictions behind the case table's −8.4-point full-text gap (40 entries; Fig. 3a), the matched ablation, the fourth reading-better arm, stopped entries put back and runs on 2–10 entries are all post hoc or exploratory, and the primary endpoint is not adjusted across the five comparisons with direct reading (Sec. 3.3). The disclosure is exemplary, but it reduces the confirmatory weight of the main comparison.

The subset-dependence claim for the evidence graph leans on a single entry (Reviewer 3). Section 4.2 and App. F report −1.2 points on the ablation's 19 entries with half or more full text and +3.1 on the other 19. The 'other 19' include the one entry with all papers in full text (App. F), on which the graph is +17.8 (Table 14); that entry alone contributes about 0.9 points (17.8/19), and the remaining 18 average about +2.3. The label 'half or more full text' also excludes this all-full-text entry, which the main text does not say.

The 'stated in the supplied text' decomposition is partly mechanical (Reviewers 2 and 3). 'Stated' requires a verbatim quote that the same model found, so facts needing inference fall into 'not stated' by construction, as the paper notes (Sec. 4.1). The contrast between 91.0–94.4% coverage of stated facts and 5.5–6.9% of facts not stated (Fig. 2c; Table 19) therefore cannot be read at face value without a manual check, and conveyance of 'not stated' facts is not separated into inference, recall and judge error.

The benchmark cannot be reused with comparable numbers (all three reviewers). The fixed fact lists contain curator wording and are not redistributed, so others must rebuild the reference and split it again (Sec. 3.1 'Reuse'; Ethics statement). How much a fresh split by the same procedure moves levels and differences was not measured, while a different splitting procedure moved levels by 2–5 points with the same ordering (Table 6; App. M.4). The writer and judge is a proprietary model called without temperature or seed control (Reproducibility statement). External users therefore cannot score a new strategy against the same denominators, which weakens contribution (1).

The released-pipeline comparison is too thin to inform the design question and its results are missing from the main text (all three reviewers). PaperQA2 ran without its agent on 10 entries, GraphRAG on 4, and STORM produced no article because the safety filter stopped its chain-of-thought prompts (App. J). The systems answered six concatenated questions rather than writing one entry, and their drafts were unrepaired against repaired strategy drafts (Limitation (xii)). Section 4.4 says the systems ran but gives none of the results (−14.5 and −13.4 points; Table 35).

The presentation is very dense and hard to follow (all three reviewers). The abstract, Sec. 1 and Secs. 4.2–4.4 pack many intervals, entry counts and status qualifiers into single sentences (e.g. the abstract's 'on all 41, it requires keeping the unrevised draft where the model's safety filter stopped the revision'; Sec. 4.4 compresses four experiments into one paragraph). Readers must carry defined terms ('like for like', 'symmetric rule', 'stopped reply', 'repaired', 'stated') across a 55-page document whose appendix (about 38 pages, 54 tables) holds much of the evidence. Some statements are not backed by shown content: the 'ten approaches reviewed' are never listed (Sec. 4.3; App. I), and the claim that about a third of curator facts concern papers free to read but not openly licensed (Sec. 4.3; App. I) has no table or method.
Questions: Can you provide expert labels on a stratified sample (for example 200–500 (fact, draft) 'conveyed' judgements across strategies and access levels, plus a sample of 'stated'/'not stated' labels), with chance-corrected agreement against the model judge? Do the order in Table 1 and the 0.5–2.6-point differences survive the observed error rate?

Can a judge from a different model family re-score at least the main comparison, the reading-better arms and the hidden-full-text experiment (or the 30 replicate entries), to test self-preference and correlated errors between the 'stated' and 'conveyed' judgements?

For the completeness pass and the merge, can you report a length-controlled comparison, for example direct reading instructed to write about 14,000 characters or to be exhaustive, or coverage per 1,000 characters, together with a precision-side estimate that has an interval and covers more than 20 audited entries?
Was medium-effort extraction with rule-assigned synopsis terms fixed before any results were seen? What does the 93-entry main comparison look like with extraction matched to the writers' effort?

How much do levels and differences move under a fresh split of the same paragraphs by the same procedure (for example on 30 entries)? Could the reference be offered in a form usable without redistributing curator wording, such as a hosted scoring service over fact identifiers?

Do safety-filter stops correlate with creation era, number of papers, full-text share, disease area, the step that was stopped, or direct reading's coverage on the same entry? Is there evidence that completed-entry comparisons are not biased by which entries are lost?

Could you test the regime in which extract-then-write or agentic designs are expected to help, for example a smaller-context writer or an artificially limited context budget on the same entries? Please also report the input-size distribution of the 100 main entries, not only of the 6 padding entries (Table 44).

Can the access effect be broken down by fact type (variant identity or notation, zygosity, counts, phenotype, inheritance, functional evidence), and does the number of facts per paragraph differ by access level? How were the atomic splits checked for granularity and consistency?
How does the evidence graph's +3.1 on the ablation's 'other 19' entries change without the single all-full-text entry (+17.8 in Table 14)?

For the 'not stated' facts that reading strategies still convey at 5.5–6.9%, can inference (for example inheritance from zygosity) be separated from recall by comparing per fact against the memory-only control? Of the variants written that OMIM does not list (111 for the graph and 130 for the case table against 36 for direct reading; Table 10), how many are reported in the cited papers?

In 22 of the 37 facts on which a draft contradicted the reference, the same model sided with the draft (App. M.3). Has a person checked any of these, and how would a non-trivial reference error rate change the interpretation of the ceiling?
Can the agentic curator's tool use be logged to confirm what it read and how many read and search calls it made per entry (App. B)?

How was 'about a third of curator facts concern papers free to read but not openly licensed' (Sec. 4.3; App. I) computed? Which were the ten approaches reviewed? Why are the released-pipeline results (Table 35) not stated in Sec. 4.4? In Table 11, the evidence-graph rows for OMIM facts conveyed and for synopsis HPO F1 (exact) report the same better/worse/tied counts (36/48/16) and sign-test p (0.230); please confirm this is not a copy error.
Limitations: The authors list twelve limitations candidly (Sec. 5). The two most consequential, the absence of human validation and of a second model family, are listed as items rather than limiting the conclusions themselves in the abstract and conclusion, and no experiment addresses either.

The conclusions hold for one proprietary long-context model, entries with 2–12 references, open-access text without supplements and a variant-centred reference. They should not be read as general statements about LLM-assisted curation or about the relative merit of retrieval, graph or agent designs, and the title and abstract framing should say so.
The reference cannot be redistributed and fresh-split stability is unmeasured, so results are comparable only as differences within one split, not as levels across studies.

Safety-filter stops are opaque, non-random and depend on the strategy; they should be treated as a first-class outcome in any deployment claim, and whether they are informative about entry difficulty is untested.
The main strategies were developed on their evaluation entries; held-out evidence is limited to 20 compared 2026 entries and the 41-entry reading-better split.

Societal: the drafts concern clinical genetics. The ethics statement properly says that a passed audit certifies neither correctness nor completeness and that drafts are not clinical guidance. It could add that the audit's over-citation and qualifier blind spots (zygosity, 'one family') are exactly the errors that matter clinically, and the abstract could state that the 94–97% 'judged supported' rates measure fidelity to the cited text, not correctness.
